questions.question: When backing with a trailer, how should you start?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want to go.
Turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
Turn the wheel as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer begins to turn, turn the wheel the opposite way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: When backing up to connect a trailer, where should the tractor be?

options.text: Straight in front of the trailer.
Lined up next to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor straight in front of the trailer when connecting. Backing at an angle could cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: How long should it take air pressure to build up in a single air system?
questions.explanation: Air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes in a single air system.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every trip. Rust around wheel nuts is a sign they may be loose.

questions.question: What is a benefit of watching the road ahead?

options.text: It is safer than only watching your mirrors.
It does not affect your safety.
It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous in a large vehicle. Looking ahead helps you see obstacles early so you can avoid them without making sudden moves.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block other drivers, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When driving slowly and blocking traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: When should you use a trolley valve?

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls the trailer brakes and should only be used for testing. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release the air pressure from the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift to a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: How should you park a truck?

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: What is a problem with rough acceleration?

options.text: It helps you stay awake on long trips.
It can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is set to "emergency"?

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will activate.
More air will go to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will activate.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: Which statement about turn signals is NOT a good rule?

options.text: Signal early, before you turn or change lanes.
Keep signaling throughout the turn or lane change.
Don't signal if no one is near you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal if no one is near you.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Keep your signal on during the turn. Turn it off only after you finish moving. You should signal even if no one is nearby.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: How do you prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?
questions.explanation: With a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. This prevents the vehicle from rolling backward.

questions.question: If a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge a train's speed accurately. Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long the trip is.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Okay if the food is easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving are dangerous distractions. Plan time to stop and eat on long trips.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.
